Scientific basis, references and limitations

Atlas and ontology. Allen Mouse Brain Common Coordinate Framework v3 and Allen structure ontology. Wang Q, Ding S-L, Li Y, et al. Cell 181, 936–953.e20 (2020). DOI: 10.1016/j.cell.2020.04.007. Allen Institute for Brain Science, Allen Mouse Brain Atlas [dataset].

Volumetric 2D source. The build tool supports the official Allen CCFv3 average-template and CCF 2017 annotation NRRDs at 25, 50 or 100 µm. It also supports Steinmetz N. Modified Allen CCF 2017 for cortex-lab/allenCCF. Figshare (2024). DOI: 10.6084/m9.figshare.25365829. CC BY 4.0.

Voxel-based 2D rendering. When installed, the coronal and sagittal views are rendered from local browser volumes derived either from the official Allen average-template and CCF 2017 annotation NRRDs or from the cortex-lab 10 µm template and by-index annotation volumes. Region identity comes from the actual annotation voxel and the 2017 structure tree, not from surface-mesh intersections. The assets are generated with tools/build_atlas_assets.py.

Stereotaxic landmarks. Cecyn MN, Abrahao KP. Where do you measure the Bregma for rodent stereotaxic surgery? IBRO Neuroscience Reports 15, 143–148 (2023). DOI: 10.1016/j.ibneur.2023.07.003.

Coordinate convention. Values are millimetres relative to bregma. Left ML is positive and right ML is negative in this application. The CCF-to-stereotaxic registration is approximate and individual brains vary with strain, age, sex, body size, fixation and surgical positioning.

Intended use. Planning and visualisation only. Do not treat the displayed region assignment or corrected dial values as a substitute for pilot injections, brain-surface depth checks, post-operative histology or local SOPs.
